body:
Working entry (chk-iqimao3h, Epoch 2 — Debts of 0.1.0–0.3.0): «Single select sized as a list box — a single select's
`size` shown as a list box of `size` rows, keys moving the choice, no popup; the founder's F4 C». Its one freight block
(`block` view, `cry-wwa3vo3b`), folded whole:

> CARRY: res-ysz67imk (a single select's `size` stays unread) is owned here, re-targeted from v040-04: the founder's
> F4 C, «Отдельной записью маршрута (Recommended)», gave it a route entry of its own so the select-list chunk did not
> grow, placed after «Engine debts» by the operator's approval of the P5 card's two Beyond-the-plan rows
> (2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts; chunks/2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts/inputs/I2-select-list-debts-founder-2026-11-20.md.txt,
> chunks/2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts/inputs/I4-relay-3.md.txt)

A single select (`select` without `multiple`) whose `size` reads a valid value above 1 shows as HTML renders it: an
in-flow list box `size` rows tall, its rows the select's options (and group headers), the chosen row marked, the rest
scrolling — not a closed box that opens the engine-painted popup list. Keys move the choice in the box, a click on a row
chooses it, and no popup opens. Residual `res-ysz67imk` is closed by it.

- Re-verified at take-up: `res-ysz67imk` (rev 2, `absorbed`, disposition `v040-04`) reads «a single select's `size`
  stays unread, `size` read on a `multiple` select alone on the founder's F8». The founder's F4 C (2026-11-20, I2
  above) gave this its own route entry; the entry exists (chk-iqimao3h) and its CARRY names the residual.

- **The founder's F8 is reversed in part.** F8 (2026-10-31-select-popup, his «Читать на multiple (Рекомендую)», option
  A) reads: «Read on a `multiple` select when written. A valid `size` makes it that many rows tall and the rest scroll.
  With no `size` it stays all rows, as built, so no existing page moves. A single select's `size` stays unread, a
  stated limit: it is always a closed box and a list.» The clause that falls is the last one: «A single select's
  `size` stays unread … it is always a closed box and a list». What stands: the `multiple` reading (a valid `size` that
  many rows tall, no `size` all rows — HTML's default of 4 rows for a `multiple` select is NOT adopted here, F8's B
  stays unchosen). The reversal is the founder's (the operator's directive at this take-up, inputs#I1).

- [inferred] The existing pieces to build on: `size_rows` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select_list.rs:128`, read
  through `parse_unsigned_integer`, capped at 65534) and its presentational-hint use
  (`packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo/presentational_hints.rs:559`, a `height` of `size` × 1.2em, today on `multiple` alone);
  the `multiple` select's key model (`press_multiple_select_key`) and row click (`click_select_row`); the single
  select's key model (`press_select_key`) and popup gate (`select_list_allowed`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:890`).

- [inferred] HTML's rule: a `select` with `multiple` or a `size` above 1 is rendered as a list box, else a drop-down
  box; `size="1"`, `size="0"` or an invalid value leave a single select a drop-down box.

- The founder ruled that this is built (F4 C). What stays his (the operator's directive, inputs#I1): any choice that
  turns what an agent or a page sees beyond HTML's own rendering of a sized single select, and F8's partial reversal.
  Research comes first; every fork of his goes into one file, `founder-forks.md` in the run dir, each with its
  measurement and every option with its cost, the recommended option first — or the file says there is none.
  Technical forks are the operator's, asked in a dialog.

- An engine change for every document, remote pages included (the security plan's select rules: «its stated limits:
  … a single select's `size` is not read»), so it rides its ratification; it crosses no new carrier, verb, argument,
  key name, result field, cause, session error, exit, log field or span unless the founder rules it.

- [inferred] Snapshot, diff, accessibility tree, lint, actions, layout and screenshot readings of the sized single
  select follow from the engine (a list box's rows are real boxes, like a `multiple` select's); a reading that would
  differ from a `multiple` list box's, or from HTML's, is a fork.
- The chunk is sized at P5: if it does not fit one implement window, the split is proposed there.

- Out of scope: HTML's default `multiple` height (4 rows); the popup list's own behaviour for an unsized single select;
  dependency and CI debts (chk-rvaqkxvd); any canvas work.

- [inferred] `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/{select,select_list}.rs`, `src/document.rs` (`select_list_allowed`),
  `src/events/{keyboard,pointer}.rs`, `src/stylo/presentational_hints.rs`, `src/accessibility.rs` (list box vs combo
  box role), the UA stylesheet for a list box's look; `packages/blitz-paint` (a single select's painted face);
  `packages/escher-driver` readers (snapshot `expanded`/`highlighted`, `type` on a select, lint, actions, layout's
  placing words).

- Checks beside `tests/blitz-tests/tests/{select_interaction,select_popup,stand_act_select,stand_act_popup}.rs`, both
  layout modes.

- `efe014e9eb3e` (HEAD, the last wrap's flip) — verdict not yet available: CI#44910526142 in progress at the take-up
  (4/4 checks, the oldest `Test [default features]` at 490 s); no red to disposition.

- **is_multiple_select** (blitz-dom) — `build_accessibility_node` @ accessibility.rs:175, `select_value` @
  document.rs:858, `handle_key_or_input_event` @ keyboard.rs:110; (dioxus-native-dom copy) `closed_select_of` @
  snapshot.rs:274, re-exported at lib.rs:55.

- **closed_select_of** — `Builder::visit` @ snapshot.rs:170, `flatten` @ escher-driver lint.rs:341, re-exported at
  dioxus-native-dom lib.rs:54 and imported at lint.rs:7: the snapshot's row bounds and the lint's overlap skip both
  follow it, so fixing it moves both.

- **select_list_allowed** — `live_select_list` @ document.rs:927, `open_select_list` @ :940,
  `reconcile_select_list` @ :1025: one gate closes the popup for a list box on open, on read and on reconcile.

- **size_rows** — `carries_valid_size` @ keyboard.rs:385, `compute_presentational_hints` @
  presentational_hints.rs:559, its unit test @ select_list.rs:474.
- **settle_select_choice** — `DocumentMutator::flush` @ mutator.rs:1241 (the one caller).
- **open_select_list** — `press_select_key` @ keyboard.rs:173 and :178, `click_select` @ pointer.rs:988.
- **click_select_row** — `click_option` @ pointer.rs:1001. **press_multiple_select_key** — keyboard.rs:115.

- **A hint on descendants from an ancestor's attribute** (presentational_hints.rs:112-125, :660-666; mutator.rs
  :816-823): `cellpadding` is read on the cell from its table, and a write to it restyles the table's descendants —
  the one mechanism that lets an attribute only a parse can judge style a select's rows.

- **Closed key match** (keyboard.rs:163-190, 258-282): every key outside the match does nothing (security

# escher — the founder's answers for «Single select sized as a list box» (answered by 2026-11-21 17:27Z)

Given by one question dialog in the overseer session (two questions), raised 2026-11-21 about 14:25Z and answered by
17:27Z, relayed by the overseer. The fork, its measurement and every option whole: the phase's
`.andromeda/runs/2026-11-21T13-54-35-phase/founder-forks.md`. Each answer is his chosen label, verbatim.

## F1 — how much of his F8 falls
The question quoted his F8 (2026-10-31, «Читать на multiple»), said his F4 C of 2026-11-20 already drops its last sentence,
gave the measurement (no `multiple` select and no sized select on the 7GUIs stand; 17 `multiple` selects in checks and
examples, 12 with no `size`) and that under the first two options his answer ratifies the engine reading `size` on a single
select in every document.

Options: only the last sentence falls (marked recommended) · F8 falls whole, HTML's rule · keep F8 whole.

His answer, the label as offered: «Падает только последняя часть (Recommended)» — the forks file's option **A**.

As the option read to him: a single select with `size` above 1 becomes a list box `size` rows tall, no popup, keys and
clicks choosing a row; a `multiple` select stays exactly as F8 built it; no existing page or check moves; the `multiple`
default stays a stated difference from HTML (4 rows there); about 17 files, one implement window.

## What the chunk takes from HTML with no fork — offered for his objection
The question listed the five: (1) HTML's display size — `size="1"`, `size="0"` and an invalid value leave a drop-down;
(2) a list box with no `selected` option starts with nothing chosen — an empty value, no form entry, no `value` in the
snapshot; (3) it reads `ListBox` with no `expanded`, the chosen row `selected` and painted in the `multiple` chosen-row
pair; (4) the arrows, Home, End and typeahead choose a row at once, Enter and Space open nothing, a click chooses one row,
Ctrl and Shift change nothing; (5) for an agent a `click` on a row is accepted and `type` chooses the first row by the
text's start, with no new word, field or refusal cause.

Options: all as HTML has it, no objection (marked recommended) · an objection, typed.

His answer, the label as offered: «Всё по HTML, возражений нет (Recommended)»

As the option read to him: Ctrl+click and Ctrl+A stay stated limits on a list box, as on a `multiple` select today.

title: Plan — 2026-11-21-single-select-sized-as-a-list-box: "Single select sized as a list box"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-11-21-single-select-sized-as-a-list-box: "Single select sized as a list box"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-21-single-select-sized-as-a-list-box · **Version:** escher-0.4.0

A single select (`select` with no `multiple`) whose HTML display size is above 1 is rendered as HTML renders it:
an in-flow list box `size` rows tall. Its options and group headers are rows, the chosen row is marked, and the rest
scroll. It opens no popup. Its keys and clicks choose a row at once, and it may stand with nothing chosen. Residual
`res-ysz67imk` («a single select's `size` stays unread») closes with it.

The founder ruled it built (his F4 C, 2026-11-20). On this chunk's one fork he chose «Падает только последняя часть
(Recommended)»: of his F8 only the last sentence falls, «A single select's `size` stays unread, a stated limit: it is
always a closed box and a list.» A `multiple` select stays exactly as F8 built it: all rows with no `size`, `size`
rows with one. To the five things the chunk takes from HTML he answered «Всё по HTML, возражений нет (Recommended)»
(inputs#I3; the fork whole: `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-21T13-54-35-phase/founder-forks.md`). His F1 answer ratifies
the engine reading a single select's `size` in every document, remote pages included: a capped number, no text
carried out, through the same `size_rows` parse a `multiple` select's `size` takes. That reading is an engine change
for every document and a boundary widening of the select's attribute reads.

The engine work extends the existing split, which today is single versus `multiple`
(architecture · decision/multiple-and-optgroup-modelled), with a third reading: **a list box**, meaning a select that
is `multiple` or whose display size is above 1 (HTML §4.10.7, display size; §15.5.15). Every arm that research's graph
query found keyed on single versus `multiple` now says which side a single list box takes:
- **The popup arms:** the gate, `click_select` and `press_select_key`.
- **The row arms:** `click_option` and the key dispatch.
- **The readers:** the tree's role and `expanded`, `layout_reason`, and the bridge's `closed_select_of`.
- **The selectedness algorithm**, which picks a first option only at display size 1.

- **The look:** presentational hints on the select and its rows, following the `cellpadding` precedent (research
  §Patterns), since no selector of the default sheet can read a parsed `size`.

The driver gains no verb, argument, key name, result field, cause, session error, exit, log field or span
(security · decision/boundary-widening-rule). Its readings follow the engine: rows with their own bounds, accepted
clicks, `ListBox` with no `expanded`. Only its `click` and `press` help and the capability statement are re-worded,
under the ratified rule for the program's own fixed text (architecture · decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers).

1. **The list-box reading** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select.rs`, beside `is_single_select` /
   `is_multiple_select` at :92-99; `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select_list.rs`, `size_rows` at :128).
   - Add a crate-private reading of a select's display size per HTML: `size` read through `size_rows` where it
     answers, else 1.
   - Add a reading `is_list_box(element)`: true for a `select` that carries `multiple` or whose display size is
     above 1.
   - `size="1"`, `size="0"`, `size="many"`, `size="-3"`, an empty value and no attribute leave a single select a
     drop-down.
   - Re-word `size_rows`'s doc from «a `multiple` select's» to «a select's».
   - Add a public read-only `BaseDocument::is_list_box(&self, select: NodeId) -> bool` in
     `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` beside `select_value`. It resolves its node through `get_node`: a stale or
     non-select id reads `false`, with no panic. Its doc cites HTML's display size.
   - Unit tests in `select.rs`'s inline test module pin the display-size table, with its row count asserted. Keeps
     tests S3 and S4; arch S5 (the spec URL at the implementation).

2. **Selectedness at display size above 1** (`settled` at `node/select.rs:262`; `settle_select_choice` at
   `document.rs:1222-1240`).
   - The fallback to the first enabled option applies only where the select's display size is 1.
   - A single list box keeps its last chosen option alone, or none.
   - `settle_select_choice` passes the select's display size, or its list-box reading, to the rule.
   - `set_option_selectedness` (`mutator.rs:1495`) keeps one chosen option on any single select, list box included.
     It is unchanged.
   - The inline table test gains rows: a list box with no `selected` chooses none; one with two `selected` keeps the
     last; a drop-down with none chooses the first enabled option, as today.

3. **A `size` write on a select** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs`: `set_attribute` :330-370, `remove_attribute`
   :530-540, `restyle_for_attribute_change` :784-830).
   - A `size` write or removal on a `select` records the select for the flush's re-settle, as a `multiple` write does
     (`record_select_of_multiple_write`). A list box turned back into a drop-down therefore chooses its first enabled
     option, HTML's invariant for display size 1.
   - The write restyles the select's descendants as a table's `cellpadding` write restyles its cells
     (`RESTYLE_DESCENDANTS`), so the rows' hints of step 4 are re-read.
   - An open list on a select that becomes a list box closes through `reconcile_select_list` once step 5's gate reads
     it.

4. **The list box's look as presentational hints** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo/presentational_hints.rs`: the
   `size` arm :553-563, the `cellpadding` ancestor read :112-125 as the pattern).
   - **On a single list box itself:** the `height` of `size` × 1.2em (the existing arm, its `multiple` gate widened
     to the list-box reading) and `overflow-y: auto`. The arm's comment «A single select's `size` stays unread: it
     is a closed box» is retired.
   - **On an `option` or `optgroup` whose select (its parent, or its group's parent) is a single list box:** the
     hints the default sheet gives a `multiple` select's rows at `assets/default.css:202-229`. That is
     `display: block` (option and optgroup), `padding: 0 2px` and `white-space: nowrap` (option), `line-height: 1.2`
     (option), and on an option reading `CHECKED` `background-color: #c8c8c8` and `color: #000000`. The pair is
     Chromium's inactive selected pair the sheet already holds (design · decision/select-chosen-row-chromium-pair).
   - A hint ranks above the user-agent sheet, so it outranks `option { display: none }`,
     `select:not([multiple]) > option:checked { display: inline }` and `select:not([multiple]) > optgroup { display:
     contents }`. A page's own rules still win.
   - `assets/default.css` is not edited: a `multiple` select keeps its selector rules as they stand.
   - No token and no colour outside the existing pair is added.

5. **No popup on a list box** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`, `select_list_allowed` :890-920, whose three
   callers are `live_select_list` :927, `open_select_list` :940 and `reconcile_select_list` :1025).
   - The gate adds «not a list box».
   - In `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs`, `click_select` (:978-990) opens a list only on a drop-down. On a
     single list box a click on the select's own box focuses it, starts its typed text afresh and opens nothing.
   - `click_label` (:1013-1030) is unchanged: it focuses any single select.

6. **A row click on a single list box** (`click_option`, `pointer.rs:995-1010`).
   - An option of a single list box takes the row arm, as a `multiple` select's does. It focuses the select, starts
     its typed text afresh and clears the text selection.
   - It chooses that row alone through `apply_select_choice`, whatever Ctrl, Meta or Shift is held.
   - A disabled select or a disabled row changes nothing.
   - A `multiple` select's row arm (`click_select_row`) is unchanged.
   - The engine's click handler stays below the complexity ceiling (test-plan · decision/complexity-ceiling-host-only,
     its except): the arm's work lives in `click_option` or a helper beside it, not in `handle_click`.

7. **A single list box's keys** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs`: the dispatch at :103-115,
   `press_select_key` :163-190).
   - A focused single list box that is no disabled form control takes its own closed key match:
     - ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End step from its chosen row through `select::stepped`. With nothing chosen,
       Next reads as First and Previous as Last.
     - A character typed with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta is typeahead through `type_into_select` and `select::matched`, as
       today.
     - The reached row becomes the choice through `apply_select_choice`, one `input` then one `change`, and is
       brought into view at once, `ScrollBehavior::Instant` and `Nearest`, as `apply_row_gesture` does
       (:405-412).
     - Enter, a Space with no typed text standing, and every other key do nothing. Shift, Ctrl or Meta held with an
       arrow change nothing beyond the plain step.
   - `press_select_key` keeps its arms for a drop-down alone, and `press_multiple_select_key` is unchanged.
   - Keeps security · decision/select-keys-closed-match and decision/select-choice-one-write-path.

8. **The tree** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs`: the role at :528-531; `expanded` and the active
   descendant at :240-256).
   - A single list box reads `Role::ListBox` (HTML-AAM `select` with display size above 1), with no
     `set_multiselectable`.
   - `expanded` and the active descendant stay written on a drop-down alone. A single list box writes neither.
   - Its chosen option reads `selected` as every select's option does, and the tree's focus stays on the select.

9. **The layout reason** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/layout_reason.rs:318-335`).
   - An option or group of a single list box reads its own placing, as a `multiple` select's rows do (`block`).
   - No placing word is added (architecture · contract/layout-reason/placed-by).

10. **The bridge's closed select** (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:262-276`).
    - `closed_select_of` answers `None` for a select `BaseDocument::is_list_box` reads true, beside its open-list arm.
    - Through it the snapshot's rows read their own client rects (`Builder::visit` @ snapshot.rs:170), and the
      driver's lint reads them as ordinary rows (`flatten` @ escher-driver lint.rs:341). Neither caller changes.
    - The function's doc is re-worded to «a select that is no list box and has no list open».
    - `is_multiple_select` stays as it is.

11. **The driver's fixed texts** (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs`: `CLICK.help` :273, `PRESS.help` :315;
    their pins in `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs:124` and `PRESS`'s pin).
    - `click`: a click on a drop-down select opens its list or closes the one standing. A click on a row of a list
      box — a `multiple` select, or a single select whose `size` is above 1 — chooses it.
    - `press`: on a single select whose `size` is above 1, the arrows, `home`, `end` and typed text choose a row and
      nothing opens.
    - The pins are re-written to the new literals.
    - `refusal.rs`'s `covered` meaning («an option of a closed select») stays true and is unchanged.
    - No verb, argument, field, cause or count moves, and the `VERBS` table holds fifteen.

12. **The capability statement** (`docs/capabilities.md`):
    - :85, a `click` on a single `select`: restated for a drop-down, a list box's row click added.
    - The `size` bullet at :293: a single select whose `size` parses above 1 is a list box that many rows tall with no
      popup; a `multiple` select stays as it reads.
    - The limit at :369, «A single select's `size` is …»: removed.
    - The statement's held counts (verbs, causes, session errors, node keys, exit statuses, the a11y leg's file count,
      stand-repeat's named targets) do not move.

13. **The engine checks** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_interaction.rs`). Each runs in both layout modes, its
    tables' row counts asserted, its expected values pinned as literals (tests S2, S3; arch S1, S3, S4).
    - (a) `a_sized_single_select_is_a_list_box_of_its_rows`:
      - A single select with `size="3"` and six options, one `selected`, is three rows tall: its client height is 3 ×
        1.2 em plus the box's border and padding, pinned as a literal.
      - Its options and groups lay out as rows, each with a box of its own.
      - It reads `Role::ListBox` with no `expanded` and no multiselectable.
      - Its chosen row reads `#000000` on `#c8c8c8` at 12.56:1 through `text_contrast`.
    - (b) `a_sized_single_select_with_nothing_chosen_reads_no_value`: with no `selected` option, `select_value` reads
      `None` and no option reads chosen. Removing `size` chooses the first enabled option, and a `size` write back to
      3 keeps that choice.
    - (c) `the_display_size_decides_list_box_or_drop_down`: a table over `size` `"1"`, `"0"`, `"many"`, `"-3"`, `""`,
      absent, `"2"` and `"3"`. It reads `is_list_box`, the tree role, and whether a click opens a list (`open_select`).
    - (d) `the_keys_of_a_sized_single_select_choose_and_scroll`: a table of ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home, End, a typed
      character, Enter, Space, Shift+ArrowDown and Ctrl+ArrowDown on a list box of eight rows sized three.
      - Each row states the chosen row after the key, the `input` and `change` counts, and the box's `scroll_top`.
      - A chosen row past the third scrolls into view, and no key opens a list.
      - A disabled row is skipped.
    - (e) `a_click_on_a_sized_single_selects_row_chooses_it_alone`: a table of a plain click, Ctrl, Meta and Shift on
      a row, a click on a disabled row and a click on a row of a disabled select. Each row states the chosen row and
      the event counts.
    - (f) `a_size_write_turns_a_drop_down_into_a_list_box_and_back`: through the mutator, a `size` write on a drop-down
      with its list open closes the list, and the rows take their boxes. Removing `size` returns the drop-down with
      its chosen option alone showing. The same holds in both layout modes (the incremental oracle's rule).
    - Keeps a11y S1 and tests S5. The shared tables in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` hold the stand's own
      roles (`("flight-type", Role::ComboBox)` at :25), and the stand's select stays unsized, so they do not move. The
      fixture's role is stated once in this check, its one reader.

14. **No popup on a list box** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup.rs`).
    - `a_sized_single_select_opens_no_list`: on a single select with `size="3"`, a click, Enter and a Space each leave
      `open_select` `None` and request no list.
    - `hostile_html` gains a single select with `size="70000"` and 2,000 options among `others`. Every box stays
      finite and no list opens.
    - `#word` (`size="many"`, single) still opens its list, pinned unchanged.

15. **The driver checks** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_select.rs`, a new page beside `rows_page` stated in the
    file since one check reads it (tests · decision/shared-fixture-pages, its except)).
    - (a) `a_sized_single_select_reads_its_role_and_rows_each_with_its_own_bounds`: the snapshot reads the select
      `ListBox` with its name and value, and each row with bounds of its own, unlike the closed select's options at
      its client rect.
    - (b) `a_click_on_a_sized_single_selects_row_is_accepted_and_chooses_it`: the diff names the select's `value` and
      the two rows' `selected`.
    - (c) `actions_lists_a_sized_single_selects_rows_with_no_covered`: each in-view row's `click` carries no cause. A
      row scrolled out of the box reads `off-screen`, as a `multiple` select's does.
    - (d) `press_on_a_sized_single_select_chooses_with_no_list_open`: `press arrow-down` on the focused select chooses
      the next row, and the snapshot reads no open list.
    - (e) `type_on_a_sized_single_select_chooses_by_the_texts_start`: `type` chooses the first row whose label starts
      with the text, with no stray click on a row.
    - The lint at boot on this page reads 0 findings (a11y S3).

16. **The `a11y` and `stand-repeat` legs** keep their membership: `select_interaction`, `select_popup` and
    `stand_act_select` are already named there (inputs#I2, the operator's answer). No leg, pin or capability count
    moves.
- none
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select.rs` — the display-size and list-box readings; selectedness at display size above 1
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select_list.rs` — `size_rows`'s doc
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo/presentational_hints.rs` — the list box's height and overflow and its rows' hints
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` — a `size` write restyles the rows and re-settles the choice
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` — the public `is_list_box`, the popup gate and the settle read the list box
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs` — a single list box's closed key match
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` — no popup on a list box; a row click chooses the row alone
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs` — a single list box reads ListBox with no expanded
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout_reason.rs` — a single list box's rows read their own placing
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` — `closed_select_of` answers none for a list box
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — the `click` and `press` help
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs` — the two help pins
- `docs/capabilities.md` — the click line, the `size` bullet and the retired limit
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_interaction.rs` — the engine checks of step 13
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup.rs` — the no-popup check and the hostile row of step 14
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_select.rs` — the driver checks of step 15
**The gates:**
- the unit tests of the three library crates the steps touch;
- the CI-script tests, for the statement's held counts;
- the `a11y` leg, which runs `select_interaction` and `stand_act_select`;
- the pre-push gate (`fast`), whose last step is the `embolden` witness of `select_popup_painted`;

- the `doc` leg, since a public doc comment is added (`is_list_box`) and `closed_select_of`'s doc changes, and `fast`
  runs no rustdoc;
- `stand-repeat`, since the three extended targets run there.

**What no step changes:** no boot path, no binary's start and no log site. The stand's markup does not change (its one
select stays unsized). `host_log`, `mcp_log` and the cold-agent pipe are not run. There is no live leg.

**Controls.** Each new check is controlled red-before-green (tests S3). After the steps are green, /implement makes
four one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries.

- Each is fired on its entry with `--no-fail-fast` reaching the case. The kill is `--timeout 1200`: a cold build of the
  entry's targets plus the case, under the entry's default.
- A `timeout` reading is not read as held. The control is re-fired once, then stopped on.
The four:

- **The popup gate blind to a list box.** In `select_list_allowed`, remove the list-box term step 5 adds. Fired on
  gate 2, case `a_sized_single_select_opens_no_list`.

- **Selectedness blind to the display size.** In `settled`, or its caller, remove the display-size condition step 2
  adds, so a list box with nothing chosen chooses its first option. Fired on gate 2, case
  `a_sized_single_select_with_nothing_chosen_reads_no_value`.

- **The rows' hints never written.** In `compute_presentational_hints`, remove the single-list-box arm of step 4.
  Fired on gate 2, case `a_sized_single_select_is_a_list_box_of_its_rows`.

- **The bridge reading a list box as closed.** In `closed_select_of`, remove the `is_list_box` term step 10 adds.
  Fired on gate 2, case `a_click_on_a_sized_single_selects_row_is_accepted_and_chooses_it` (its row then reads
  `covered`).

Step 14's `#word` pin and the stand's flight-booker readings guard behaviour no step changes, so they take no
control.

The diff is not OS-sensitive: no `cfg` site is added. The operator's hygiene, push and CI entries stand because this
chunk's verdict reads a CI run, as every chunk's does.

body:
- (engine) Its keys:
  - ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home, End and typeahead choose a row at once, through the one write path (one `input` then
    one `change`; a choice of the chosen row fires nothing), the row brought into view;
  - Enter, Space and every other key do nothing.

  A row click chooses that row alone whatever modifier is held, and a disabled row or select changes nothing. Pinned
  by step 13 (d)–(e) (security · decision/select-choice-one-write-path, decision/select-keys-closed-match).

- (engine) A `size` write moves a select between list box and drop-down. It closes an open list, and a drop-down left
  with nothing chosen settles to its first enabled option. Pinned by step 13 (b) and (f) (security ·
  decision/single-select-selectedness).

- (engine) A `multiple` select reads as before: no step changes its sheet rules, keys or row clicks. The companions'
  entry `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --no-fail-fast --test select_popup_painted --test stand_act_popup …` and
  the existing `multiple` rows of `select_interaction` read green.

- (stand) The stand's readings do not move: the flight booker's unsized `flight-type` keeps its popup, the cross-OS
  digests hold, the boot lint reads zero. Pinned by `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh stand-repeat` and the companions'
  entry (layout-templates · decision/flight-type-select-boot-reading, decision/stand-lints-clean-at-boot).

- (docs) `docs/capabilities.md` no longer states the single-select `size` limit and states the list box. Its held
  counts are unmoved: `python3 .github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` green.

- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast`, `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` and `bash
  .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh a11y` exit 0; CI on the chunk's pushed HEAD reads `verdict: green`.

- External inputs: inputs#I1 (the operator's directive), inputs#I2 (the operator's technical answer), inputs#I3 (the
  founder's answers). F8's text is from `chunks/2026-10-31-select-popup/inputs/I5-founder-forks.md.txt` §F8.

- Research files inspected: `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select.rs`, `node/select_list.rs`,
  `stylo/presentational_hints.rs`, `assets/default.css`, `mutator.rs`, `document.rs`, `events/keyboard.rs`,
  `events/pointer.rs`, `accessibility.rs`, `layout_reason.rs`, `stylo/dom.rs`; `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs`,
  `dioxus_document.rs`; `packages/escher-driver/src/{execute,lint,schema,refusal}.rs`; `docs/capabilities.md`;
  `tests/blitz-tests/tests/{select_popup,stand_act_select}.rs`.

- **Attribute selectors in `default.css`** such as `select[size]:not([size="1"])`: rejected. A selector cannot parse
  `size`, so `size="many"`, `" 2"` or `"+2"` would style a select the engine's own arms read as a drop-down. Stylo's
  pseudo-class set is closed (stylo/dom.rs:274-325).

- **Re-using `press_multiple_select_key` or `click_select_row` as they stand**: rejected. Their Shift and Ctrl
  gestures span and flip, and a single select holds one choice.

- **HTML's 4-row default for a `multiple` select**: not built. It is the founder's F1 A (inputs#I3) and stays a stated
  difference from HTML.

- **Ctrl+click toggling and Ctrl+A on a list box**: not modelled. They stay stated limits, as on a `multiple` select
  (inputs#I3).

- **A new placing word, node key, field or cause** for a list box: none. Its readings stay inside the existing closed
  sets.

- **Every arm keyed on single versus `multiple`**, from the graph query
  (`tree-query-2026-11-21-single-select-sized-as-a-list-box.json`, row 1). `is_single_select` has 8 callers, each
  checked:
  - **Answered by a step:** `select_list_allowed` (step 5), `settle_select_choice` (2), the key dispatch (7),
    `click_select` (5), the tree (8).
  - **Unchanged:** `select_value` (a list box's choice is a single choice), `click_label`, `set_option_selectedness`.

- **Re-settle on a `size` write.** HTML's invariant that a display-size-1 select always holds a choice is why a `size`
  removal re-settles (step 3). Without it, a list box with nothing chosen turned into a drop-down would show an empty
  box.

- **A hint ranks above the user-agent sheet** in Stylo's cascade (the presentational-hints level, architecture ·
  decision/legacy-attributes-as-pres-hints). The rows' `display: block` therefore outranks the sheet's
  `display: none` and `display: inline` without editing the sheet, and a page's own rules still outrank both.

- **The chosen row's colours re-read on a choice.** An option's `CHECKED` change already restyles it through the
  sheet's `:checked` selectors, so its hints are re-read then.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):** the founder's F1 A answer (inputs#I3) is the boundary-widening ratification. The
  playbook's *Boundary widening* pattern (`rul-izni57qv`) applies: his own word, relayed by the overseer.
  - architecture · decision/select-size-hint — a single select's `size` read for its display size: above 1, a list
    box; the «stays unread» clause retired.
  - architecture · decision/single-select-list-opening, decision/select-list-painted-overlay — narrowed to a
    drop-down.
  - architecture · decision/hit-focus-form-engine-changes — the list box joins the tally, flagged upstreamable.
  - architecture · contract/dioxus-native-dom/closed-select-of, contract/accessibility-tree/select-expanded,
    contract/driver-verbs/click — the list box.
  - security-plan · decision/single-select-selectedness — its except «a single select's size is not read» retired,
    nothing chosen allowed at display size above 1.
  - security-plan · decision/multiple-select-size-rows, decision/select-size-hint-cap, decision/select-list-open-gate
    — widened to a single list box, the ratification recorded.
  - a11y-plan · contract/accessibility-tree/select-role, decision/single-select-expanded-from-list,
    contract/select-closed-list/enter-space — ListBox for a single list box, no expanded, no open.
  - design-system · decision/single-select-box-shows-chosen-label, decision/selects-that-open-no-list,
    decision/select-chosen-row-chromium-pair — a single list box's rows and chosen pair.
  - obs-plan · decision/select-size-attribute-read — the `size` read on a single select too, carrying no text out.
  - test-plan — the single-select `size` limit retired from the scope summary's limits.
  - `matrix#v040-04 notes` — 2026-11-21 (2026-11-21-single-select-sized-as-a-list-box): residual `res-ysz67imk`
    closed; a single select with `size` above 1 is a list box, on the founder's F1 A.

**Chunk:** a single select with `size` above 1 shown as an in-flow list box, keys and clicks choosing, no popup
**Date:** 2026-11-21
**Run:** 2026-11-21T17-41-12-implement

- **Files:** `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select.rs` · `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select_list.rs` ·
  `packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo/presentational_hints.rs` · `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` ·
  `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` · `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs` ·
  `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` · `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs` ·
  `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout_reason.rs` · `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` ·
  `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` · `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs` · `docs/capabilities.md` ·
  `tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_interaction.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup.rs` ·
  `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_select.rs` (16 modified, 0 new; basis `gate.py scope`: changed 16 · listed 16)

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - new public `BaseDocument::is_list_box(&self, select: NodeId) -> bool` (`document.rs` 866-875): a select with
    `multiple`, or whose display size (its `size` through `size_rows`, else 1) is above 1. It is read-only and
    resolves through `get_node`, so a stale or non-select id reads `false`. Its one non-test caller is
    `closed_select_of`.
  - new crate-private readings in `node/select.rs`: `display_size` (101-108), `is_list_box` (110-117),
    `is_single_list_box` (119-122) and `is_drop_down` (124-128). `select_holding` is made `pub(crate)`; its new
    caller is the row hints.
  - changed `select::settled(options, display_size)`: it falls back to the first enabled option only at display
    size 1, so a list box may stand with nothing chosen. Its one caller is `settle_select_choice`.
  - `select_list_allowed` gates on `is_drop_down` in place of `is_single_select`. Its three callers are unchanged:
    `live_select_list`, `open_select_list` and `reconcile_select_list`.
  - `click_select` opens a list on a drop-down alone. `click_option` sends a single list box's row to a new
    private `click_list_box_row` (`pointer.rs` 1153-1168), which focuses the select, clears its typeahead and the
    text selection, and chooses the row alone through `apply_select_choice`, whatever modifier is held. A
    disabled select or row changes nothing. A `multiple` select's `click_select_row` is unchanged.
  - new private `press_list_box_key` (`keyboard.rs` 198-228): a closed key match for a focused single list box
    that is no disabled form control. The arrows, Home and End step through `select::stepped`. A character with
    no Ctrl, Alt or Meta is typeahead through `select::matched` (a Space only while typed text stands). The
    reached row is scrolled into view (`Instant`, `Nearest`) and chosen through `apply_select_choice`. Enter and
    every other key do nothing. `press_select_key` is now reached by a drop-down alone, and
    `press_multiple_select_key` is unchanged.
  - the tree: a select reads `Role::ListBox` where `select::is_list_box` holds, else `Role::ComboBox`.
    `expanded` and the active descendant are written on a drop-down alone. A single list box reads neither, nor
    an author `aria-expanded`. No `set_multiselectable` on it.
  - `layout_reason`'s `select_reason`: an option of a list box reads its own placing (`BaseDocument::is_list_box`
    replaces the `multiple` read). No placing word is added.
  - `closed_select_of` (dioxus-native-dom, public) answers `None` for a select `BaseDocument::is_list_box` reads
    true. Its callers `Builder::visit` (snapshot) and escher-driver `lint`'s `flatten` are unchanged.
  - the driver's `CLICK.help` and `PRESS.help` texts are re-worded (fixed program text; verb, argument, field,
    cause and count unchanged).
  - new private `ListBoxRows` and the `declarations` and `list_box_row_hints` / `list_box_chosen_hints` helpers
    in `presentational_hints.rs` (81-132). `PresentationalHints` gains a field, `list_box_rows`.

- **Dependencies:** none.
- **Schema / config:** none. No log field, span, scrub shape, env var, port or socket.
- **Spec-master edits:** none.

- **Retired:**
  - the stated limit «a single select's `size` is unread». It is gone from `docs/capabilities.md`'s `select`
    model limits and from the `size` presentational-hint arm's comment.
  - residual `res-ysz67imk`, carried by this entry, is built and is the wrap's to close.

- **Counts / qualifiers moved:**
  - `select_interaction` 18 → 24 tests, `select_popup` 27 → 28, `stand_act_select` 11 → 17. Basis: the `test
    result` lines of `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test {name}` at this run's first and last readings.
    `.claude/rules/a11y.md` states 18, 25 and 10.
  - The driver's verb, cause, node-key and exit counts and the a11y leg's file count are unmoved
    (`test_capability_statement.py` green).
  - qualifier: a single select's `size` is read in every document, a drop-down being a select of display size 1.
- **Dev-tool versions:** none.
- **Harness / gate surface:** none.

- **Cross-project / external claims:**
  - inputs#I1 · relay · the operator's directive at take-up (the founder's choices, the forks file, technical
    forks by dialog).
  - inputs#I2 · relay · the operator's answer to extend the existing select checks rather than add new targets.
    Followed: the checks are in `select_interaction`, `select_popup` and `stand_act_select`.
  - inputs#I3 · sibling `../additional/escher-overseer/relays/single-select-list-box-founder-2026-11-21.md` · the
    founder's F1 A (only F8's last sentence falls) and no objection to the five HTML leans. It is the ratification
    this change rides.
  - No CI run was read by this run.

  - The plan, step 15 and its a11y S3 tag: «The lint at boot on this page reads 0 findings». Measured: the
    list-box page, whose check (c) needs two of its five rows scrolled out of the size-3 box, lints 4 findings at
    boot — `fx-s-four` clipped and truncated (2px of it showing in the box's padding), and `fx-s-five` truncated
    and off-screen. That is the lint's reading of any scrolling box's hidden rows. There is no `overlap`.
    Evidence: `stand_act_select::a_sized_single_selects_page_lints_only_its_rows_scrolled_out_at_boot`.
  - The plan's Controls prose: removing the list-box term from `select_list_allowed` turns

    (`{work_dir}/evidence/control-1.txt`). Every open path already reads `is_drop_down`, and a `size` write moves

- **In-process harness (measured):** `blitz-test-harness::Harness` — construct (`from_html`, `from_component`, `from_component_alone(component, props maker, options)` — one component mounted as the one child of an anonymous root, its props a maker run once in that root's scope, riding `from_vdom` and adding no carrier, `vdom_alone` its public mount, on which a caller provides a root context before the harness builds —, `from_vdom` — which, before its one pump, provides `SeededRandom::from_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)` as a root context where the vdom's root holds none, a root context the builder gave standing; `screenshot`, `screenshot_rect`, `text_contrast` and `settle` never moving it; `wrap(doc)` keeping the clock the document's own config gave it; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), `settle` (that pass repeated until no work is due: `Settled`, or `NotSettled` naming the busy class — `Loads` at once when a request is in flight or a render-blocking resource is pending after a quiet pass, else `Render`, `Loads` or `Layout` read off the last pass at the 64-pass bound; no clock read but the harness's, no time advanced, no load waited on; the crate-private load counter forwarding `NetHandler::error` to the handler it wraps, so a failed stylesheet reaches the document, stops counting as a pending render-blocking resource and does not read `NotSettled { busy: Loads }`, and the driver's `settle_waiting` returns where it would otherwise have run to `LOAD_WAIT`), input helpers that pump, inspection (`query`, `layout_rect`, `text_content`, `focused`, `hit`, `dom_string`; - Assert first that the fixture produces the condition under test, then the behaviour; a focus test pins the node focus lands on, never only that a hidden control is not focused (the post-layout focus fixup makes that hold with or without the change under test); a new check is controlled — a named mutation of what it guards turns it red, a case it leaves green widened until it does, and the restored tree reads green; a check never derives its expected value from the constant its mutation control changes, but pins the measured value as a literal (a pixel-row pin that font-embolden moves is pinned as a stated band with its reason in a comment where the test crate cannot see the feature, its wholly-inside assertions kept exact); a control that removes a bound loosens it to twice the budget rather than removing it, so the mutated run stays bounded; a control of a read that must change nothing gives the read pending work that a pass would apply, so a read that ran a pass would be seen (a pump on a settled screen is invisible).

- Blitz-dom unit tests build DOM by hand through `DocumentMutator` — blitz-html would be a circular dev-dependency. A Dioxus fixture select whose choice a check moves is written as a controlled select (a fixture's `selected` literal is re-written on any re-render of its component, re-seeding the choice).

- `dom_string()` is a stable one-node-per-line serialization with geometry (`<div #box .a .b> @ (20,10) 100x50`) — the snapshot-style assertion surface. Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot `screenshot()` and `screenshot_rect(PixelRect)` return a `Raster` or a `ScreenshotError` (`FontsUnavailable`, `EmptyRect`): each resolves at the harness's own time (no tick, no pump), paints the viewport at its scale and device size into `VelloCpuImageRenderer` over opaque white, clips a rectangle to the viewport (an empty one `EmptyRect`), and refuses a document whose `can_paint_text` reads false with nothing painted. Since 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness `text_contrast(NodeId)` returns `Option<TextContrast>` (`text`, `background`, `ratio`, `font_size_px`, `font_weight`; `required_ratio` 3.0 for large text, else 4.5), reading and changing nothing (no mutation, input, pump or settle): the text-bearing element's computed `color`, font size and weight over the background composited source-over from its ancestors' `background-color`s onto the root-else-`body` canvas over opaque white, `None` with no text or where an element on the walk has `opacity` below 1, a filter, a background image or a `mix-blend-mode` other than `normal`; `highlight_contrast(NodeId)` returns `Option<TextContrast>` for the highlighted row of an open select list alone — the list's highlight text and background through the one contrast formula, the option's own font size and weight — `None` for any other node, reading and changing nothing; `contrast_ratio` is the WCAG 2.x ratio. With no node focused, the harness's focused reading answers the root `html` element, never none, so a check that a click clears focus asserts the root element. A check asking whether a node has a box reads the node's computed display beside its client rect (a node a restyle turns `display: none` keeps the client rect it last laid out at).
